summary.intent: Run Session 5 of the LAUNCH-v1-alpha plan, starting with WP E: introduce a NativeName type so registry-equivalent package names (PyPI PEP 503, Cargo case and -/_) are treated as one identity, with WP I (dir index for relative workspace:) to follow.
summary.outcome: Implemented NativeName in callisto-model and migrated the graph crate (walk owner admission, identity index, config rule matching, history name checks) so equivalent names now fail loading with E100. Added boundary tests, updated docs/spec and a changeset, applied review fixes, and committed. WP I was not started, and no push or mutants run appears in the transcript.

repo: Worktree-based workflow: Session work happens in .claude/worktrees/wp-e-native-name off origin/main; fetching needs github.com allowed in the sandbox.
Gate commands are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`; a gate script wrapped them and the first run failed only on formatting, fixed by `cargo fmt --all`.
Changesets are created with `cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add --package cargo/callisto-cli:patch --summary ...`, with a bold headline, Why it matters, Action and Limits structure.
Builds use CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 to limit resource use.

Cross-ecosystem fallbacks and bare selectors must stay exact-spelling matches; only qualified selectors (ecosystem/name) apply registry equivalence. Review caught that the initial implementation over-applied equivalence.
ReleasePackageId.name deliberately stays a String: keying it on NativeName would reorder serialized rosters and could make a stored decision match a renamed package.

The plan's claims about Cargo equivalence code and a settled decision were unverified by the design subagent: check_cargo_name only validates characters, and no memory backed the decision that Cargo foo-bar/foo_bar is E100.

code.finding: New NativeName struct (ecosystem, spelling, key) with hand-written Eq/Hash/Ord on (ecosystem, key); the key is the PEP 503 form for PyPI, lowercase with _ to - for Cargo, and exact for others.
native_owner and path_native_keys are now keyed on NativeName, which is the actual duplicate-detection fix.
native_in_ecosystem becomes a single get returning Option; the PyPI ambiguity Err path is removed because E100 now prevents equivalent-name collisions.
rule_applies now compares NativeName values, which fixes [[package]] rule matching for equivalent spellings.
names_equal was deleted in favor of NativeName equality.

workflow: Delegating a read-only design to a subagent surfaced false premises in the plan before any code was written. Its report was treated as input, not as authority.
Bulk refactors by Python/perl regex scripts needed several rounds of compiler-driven cleanup, and BSD sed on macOS lacks GNU in-place syntax (the Edit tool or perl works).
Writing the boundary test first against the real Workspace::load avoids testing only helper functions.

friction: BSD sed `-i` syntax failed on macOS, forcing a switch to the Edit tool or perl.
Regex-based mass rewrites of tuple keys to NativeName::new broke some test lookups that needed reverting or manual fixes, taking several clippy iterations.
The first pre-push gate failed on formatting only.
The initial implementation applied equivalence to bare and cross-ecosystem lookups, which review flagged as too broad.
open_items: Glob patterns (PackagePattern::matches_native, pattern.rs:72) still match on the manifest spelling, so pypi/my-* does not match My_Pkg; needs a code comment or tracked follow-up.
The owner should confirm that Cargo foo-bar/foo_bar should be E100, since no existing code or memory enforced it.
The owner should decide whether the new E100 rejection counts as **Breaking:** in the changeset; it is currently a patch.
The E102 'did you mean' candidate order may change for mixed-case names, so insta snapshots should be checked.
WP I (dir index for relative workspace:) remains for Session 5, and mutants, push and trail steps were not yet done.
